summary: Karl Benedikt Hase worked in linguistics and other fields after studying at the universities of Helmstedt and Jena. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Halle and Leipzig, completing his doctorate under Georg Curtius. He worked at the Russian Institute of Classical Philology, the University of Freiburg, and spent decades as professor at Leipzig.

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, the 10th Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1842 to 1845.
Karl Eugen Neumann worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1887 to 1889 and completed his doctorate under Richard Pischel around 1890–1891.
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. From circa 1856 to 1882, he held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University, where he later served as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from circa 1892 to 1925.

Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch, Georg von der Gabelentz, Friedrich Max Müller, and Tetsujiro Inoue. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Geldner studied Indology, Iranian, and Central Asian linguistics at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Tübingen, Halle, Berlin, and Marburg.
Karl G. Heider is a scholar who completed his studies at Williams College, Harvard College, and Harvard University between 1952 and 1966.

Karl H. Potter was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of California and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at the University of Minnesota and the University of Washington.

Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst. He held chairs at Saarland University and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and was a Bavarian Academy of Sciences member.

Karl Jettmar was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Vienna, he worked at Weltmuseum Wien, the Frobenius Institute, and the universities of Vienna, Mainz, and Heidelberg.

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann, a scholar of philosophy and Indology, studied at Mainz and Würzburg. He held posts at Gymnasium Aschaffenburg, Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg, Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg, and the University of Bonn.
Karl Lachmann, a scholar in linguistics and other fields, studied at the universities of Leipzig and Göttingen. He later held a position at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1825 to 1851.

Karl Marbe worked in linguistics and other fields, having studied at the University of Bonn. He later held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt from circa 1905 to 1909 and the University of Würzburg from circa 1909 to 1935.

Karl Müllenhoff was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kiel University, the University of Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at Kiel University and Frederick William University Berlin.

Karl Otfried Müller was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Boeckh, Schleiermacher, and Wolf. He held posts at Magdalenaeum Wrocław and served as a professor at the University of Göttingen.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury, the London School of Economics, King's College London, and the University of London.
